<security_assessment>
<decision>UNSAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD contains a top-level `main` function call (`main`) outside of any function definition. This means that when the PKGBUILD is sourced during `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, the `main` function will be executed immediately as part of the global scope.

Inside `main`, there is a loop that uses `eval` to dynamically construct and execute `package_` functions. The use of `eval` with untrusted or dynamically constructed strings is inherently dangerous, especially when combined with variables that are derived from potentially external inputs (like URLs and package names). While the immediate intent appears to be code generation for packaging, the use of `eval` on data-driven strings could allow for arbitrary code execution if any of the underlying arrays (`_pkgdescs`, `_urls`, `_depends`, `_optdepends`) were manipulated.

More critically, this execution occurs at parse time due to the unguarded `main` call, meaning that simply running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` triggers code evaluation — which violates the expected safe parsing behavior. This constitutes a supply-chain risk because it allows execution of potentially malicious logic without user interaction during what should be a metadata-only operation.

This is not standard PKGBUILD practice; functions like `package()` should be defined statically and called by `makepkg` at the appropriate stage, not generated via `eval` and triggered at parse time.
</details>

The `build()` function and the internals of the generated `package_*()` functions are out of scope for this gate (they run later), but nothing in the global scope or inside `main()` presents a risk during `makepkg --printsrcinfo`.
